note: Explanatory slides for the journal club. Figures marked 'schematic' are illustrations, not data from the paper.

slides.title: The a-theorem
text: In four dimensions the coefficient $a$ of the Euler density in the trace anomaly counts degrees of freedom. Komargodski and Schwimmer proved that it decreases between UV and IR fixed points.

figure.caption: Renormalisation-group flows from a UV to an IR conformal field theory.
figure.note: weak theorem: only a_UV > a_IR at the endpoints

slides.title: Local RG and the Jack–Osborn metric
text: Making couplings spacetime-dependent, Jack and Osborn found a function $\tilde a$ that interpolates between $a_{\rm UV}$ and $a_{\rm IR}$, and a metric $\chi_{IJ}$ on the space of couplings:
bullets: If $\chi_{IJ}$ is positive, $\tilde a$ is monotonic along the flow: the strong a-theorem
In perturbation theory $\chi_{IJ}>0$; beyond it, positivity was open

slides.title: The averaged null energy condition
text: Integrated along a complete light ray, the energy density measured by any observer is non-negative in every unitary QFT.

figure.caption: The light-ray operator $\mathcal E$ acts like a calorimeter placed along a null line.

slides.title: A non-perturbative metric
text: The authors build $\chi_{IJ}$ from the three-point function of two relevant operators with the averaged null energy, and decompose it under null rotations that fix the light ray.

slides.title: Consequence: the strong a-theorem
bullets: ⇒ $\tilde a$ decreases monotonically along the whole flow, not only between endpoints
An explicit monotonic function along the flow

figure.caption: Strong version: the interpolating function decreases at every step of every flow.
figure.note: strong theorem: ã decreases monotonically along the flow
